previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 31-year-old woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, asthma, and GERD was admitted for dyspnea and thickened green tracheal secretions. She reported difficulty breathing through her tracheostomy stoma, which she believed had partially closed, and decreased oral fluid intake. Vital signs were stable, and physical exam showed a clean trach site with clear lungs. Lab results were normal, and chest imaging revealed no acute cardiopulmonary abnormalities. She was treated with humidified oxygen, IV fluids for hydration, and guaifenesin to loosen secretions. Symptoms improved significantly by the next morning, and the planned inpatient bronchoscopy was deferred to outpatient follow-up with interventional pulmonology. No medication changes were made during admission. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue current medications and attend scheduled follow-up.

___ 09:10AM BLOOD HCG-<___ year-old W with hx of tracheobronchomalacia presents with 
pain and dysphagia since supraglottoplasty at Mass Eye and Ear 
four days prior. Interventional Pulmonology performed a flexible 
bronchoscopy and found severe supraglottic edema with scarring 
of the right aryepiglottic fold. ENT performed a flexible 
digital distal-chip video nasolaryngoscopic evaluation and 
reported a baseline poor-appearing airway and findings typical 
of post-procedure, with no need for additional intervention and 
instructions to follow up with her surgeon in one week. She was 
evaluated by Speech, who, after a video-assisted swallow study, 
recommended regular solid diet with thin liquids.

# Dysphagia: Per report, the patient often experiences the 
sensation of dysphagia and pain post tracheostomy changes or 
airway procedures. This is likely secodary to soft tissue 
swelling. Throughout her admission she never exhibited any signs 
of respiratory distress, nor signs of infection. She was 
evaluated by Interventional Pulmonology, ENT, and Speech (as 
above). She was NPO until safely cleared and then was started on 
a regular diet without difficulty. Per protocol she was 
monitored on telemetry without any events. She was discharged 
with follow up with her primary care physician and surgeon (Dr. 
___. 
.
# Pain: The patient's pain was controlled with small doses of IV 
morphine while NPO, then transitioned to liquid tylenol with 
codeine when tolerating PO. This is what she was taking for the 
pain at home after her procedure. 
.
# Chronic Bronchitis/Asthma: We continued the patient's home 
regimen of Montelukast (held when NPO) and Albuterol nebs every 
6 hours as needed. 
.
# Gastroesophageal reflux disease: The patient was placed on IV 
pantoprazole 40 daily while NPO, then transitioned to her home 
regimen of PO omeprazole and ranitidine.
.
# Depression: The patient's home Fluoxetine was initially held 
while NPO, then continued when cleared to begin her regular 
diet.

radiology_notes.text:
PA AND LATERAL CHEST ___ AT 0749 HOURS.

HISTORY:  History of tracheobronchomalacia with recent trach upsizing,
presenting with odynophagia and dysphagia since procedure and increased
secretions.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  Consistent with the given history, a tracheostomy is present.  A
Port-A-Cath is noted in stable position and course from a left subclavian
approach.  Lung volumes are slightly improved with no definite focal
consolidation or superimposed edema noted.  The cardiac silhouette is within
normal limits for size.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  A
slight levoconcave curvature of the thoracic spine is again evident.

IMPRESSION:  No focal lung opacity to suggest an underlying pneumonia or
aspiration.  Tracheostomy and left subclavian central line as above.

HISTORY:  ___ female with tracheobronchomalacia.  Patient now presents
with complaints of dysphagia and severe odynophagia for three days.

COMPARISON:  None available.

TECHNIQUE:  Oropharyngeal swallowing videofluoroscopy was performed in
conjunction with speech and swallow division.  Multiple consistencies of
barium were administered.

FINDINGS:  Barium passes freely through the oropharynx and esophagus without
evidence of obstruction.  The patient had mild aspiration with pureed
material, which eventually cleared when thin liquids were administered. 
Absent vocal cord movement was noted bilaterally.  For details, please refer
to speech and swallow division note in OMR.

IMPRESSION:  Mild aspiration with pureed substances.  No other evidence of
penetration or aspiration was seen.  Please see speech and swallow note for
further details.
